text: The Eiffel Tower is a wrought-iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, France. It is named after the engineer Gustave Eiffel, whose company designed and built the tower from 1887 to 1889.
Paris is the capital and most populous city of France, located on the river Seine. Major landmarks include the Eiffel Tower, the Louvre Museum, and Notre-Dame Cathedral.
The Louvre is the world's most-visited museum, located on the Right Bank of the Seine in Paris, France. It houses the Mona Lisa and the Venus de Milo.
France, officially the French Republic, is a country in Western Europe. Its capital is Paris and its population is over 67 million.

Mount Everest is Earth's highest mountain above sea level, located in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range of the Himalayas on the border between Nepal and the Tibet Autonomous Region of China. Its peak is 8,848.86 metres above sea level.
The Great Wall of China is a series of fortifications built across the historical northern borders of ancient Chinese states. The total length of all sections ever built is over 21,000 kilometres.
The Amazon rainforest is a moist broadleaf tropical rainforest in the Amazon biome that covers most of the Amazon basin of South America. It spans nine countries and most of it is in Brazil.
Apollo 11 was the American spaceflight that first landed humans on the Moon. Commander Neil Armstrong and lunar module pilot Buzz Aldrin landed the Apollo Lunar Module Eagle on July 20, 1969.

Water is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula H2O. At standard temperature and pressure it is tasteless and odorless, and freezes into ice at 0 degrees Celsius and boils into vapor at 100 degrees Celsius.

The Sun is the star at the center of the Solar System. It is a nearly perfect ball of hot plasma, heated to incandescence by nuclear fusion reactions in its core. It radiates energy mainly as visible light, ultraviolet light, and infrared radiation.
